summary: Verified IDOR security fix on GET /api/ecps/{ecp_id}. All 13 backend tests passed. Detail endpoint now enforces the same ecp_filter_for_role(user) scope as the list endpoint. Verified: (1) OWNER/MANAGER/LEAD/ACCOUNTS list/detail parity; (2) DISPATCH gets 404 for non-DISPATCH stages and 200 with scrubbed project_price + empty payments for DISPATCH stage ECPs; (3) REGISTRATION restricted to REGISTRATION_1/REGISTRATION_2/NET_METERING stages; (4) INSTALLATION_MEMBER restricted to INSTALLATION/NET_METERING AND responsible_user == self; (5) COMPLAINT gets 404 for any ECP id (empty list also); (6) Non-existent ECP id returns 404 for authorized user.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in get_ecp() correctly reuses ecp_filter_for_role() ensuring list/detail scope parity — no drift risk.
The __none__ sentinel is handled explicitly with an early 404 to avoid an unnecessary DB query; good defensive check.
DISPATCH scrubbing (_scrub_dispatch + payments=[]) is preserved after the scope check — correct order.
seed_data_creation: None; used existing OWNER-visible ECPs to discover ids across stages and roles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_ecp_detail_scope.py covers list/detail scope parity for all roles including OWNER/MANAGER/LEAD/ACCOUNTS/REGISTRATION/DISPATCH/INSTALLATION_MANAGER/INSTALLATION_MEMBER, COMPLAINT 404 blocking, DISPATCH stage-only, REGISTRATION allowed stages, INSTALLATION_MEMBER assignment gating, and non-existent id 404. Reuse for regression.
rca of the issue: Previous get_ecp() queried by id only, ignoring role scope, allowing users to fetch ECPs outside their permitted stage/assignment via direct id (classic IDOR). Fix injects ecp_filter_for_role(user) into the find_one query and pre-empts the blocked-role case with an explicit 404, matching list_ecps semantics.
